Hooks in hip-hop proved dominant with Dr Dre, Blackstreet, Mark Morrison, Toni Braxton and the Fugees all scoring huge hits. Britpop was still booming, with Oasis continuing to dominate singles sales with Sleeper hot on their heels. Global dance classics were born courtesy of Faithless and Robert Miles, and add into the mix the awesome arrival of Spice Girls, plus many more, and it’s not a year to miss. Artists featured include Spice Girls, Suede, The Fugees, Babylon Zoo, Beautiful South, Mark Morrison, Sleeper, Los Del Rio, Peter Andre, Alanis Morrisette, Manics, Dr Dre, Blackstreet, Robret Miles, Space, OMC, Garbage, Gina G, Kula Shaker, Toni Braxton, Babybird and Oasis.

programme.title: Oasis – Live at Manchester City Stadium
programme.desc: Oasis, one of the world's biggest touring bands pulls out all the stops during their 2005 world tour. Following the release of a sixth studio album, they return to their hometown of Manchester for a triumphant concert at the City of Manchester Stadium. The performance includes Lyla, Songbird, The Importance of Being Idle, Live Forever, Don’t Look Back in Anger, Cigarettes and Alcohol, Rock 'n' Roll Star and a raucous version of The Who’s classic anthem My Generation.

programme.title: Oasis - Right Here, Right Now
programme.desc: First broadcast in 1997, this documentary gives the band's account of their previous year. Featuring exclusive performances and detailed interviews with the Gallaghers.

programme.title: No Bears
programme.desc: A dissident film-maker who is trying to direct a movie in Turkey while being forced to remain in a nearby Iranian border town finds himself embroiled in a local scandal.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: The Porthcawl crew’s training night is disrupted when a call comes from a dog walker who has spotted a surfer in trouble below the cliffs at nearby Rest Bay. During the peak of a cyclone known as Storm Amy, Bridlington’s lifeboat is tasked to a Dutch trawler that has lost power 13 miles off the Yorkshire coast. In Ireland, an urgent call comes in to the Crosshaven crew from a yacht taking part in a local race; on board, an elderly sailor is reported to have broken his leg. The Calshot crew face a tense search in thick fog for a motorboat with engine failure - somewhere in the busy shipping lanes of the Solent. And reports of a submerged car in the Thames put the Chiswick crew on red alert.

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: After discovering that the person responsible for Ricardo’s death is someone close to him, Michael scrambles for a way to protect them from the consequences – without jeopardising Diana.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In this year’s Countryfile Ramble for BBC Children in Need, Matt Baker, Anita Rani, Margherita Taylor, Joe Crowley and John Craven lace up their walking boots to meet inspirational young people whose lives have been transformed through support from BBC Children in Need. The ramble is returning for its 12th year, set against the stunning backdrop of the Peak District. The presenters walk alongside five remarkable young people who have faced significant challenges, hearing first-hand how BBC Children in Need-funded projects have helped them build confidence, resilience and hope for the future.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie is in Aberdeenshire, visiting Scotland’s first inclusive farm, built by a blind farmer who is determined to make agriculture accessible for all. Arlene sails to Jura to see how the locals cope with the huge deer population and find new outlets for venison. Anne discovers how the shortage of affordable rural housing is being tackled in the Highlands. And Shahbaz is on the shores of Loch Linnhe near Fort William to see the stranded fishing boat that has become a local landmark.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek is island-hopping in this round-up of his favourite Welsh island walks. He goes wild in west Wales as he sails to Skomer Island – a national nature reserve of international importance due to its seabirds - where he gets a close-up view of the puffins, razorbills and guillemots before staying up late to see the Manx shearwater. Next, Derek goes to Flat Holm Island, where he braves a huge colony of seagulls and discovers more about the island's past, including some Victorian gun placements. Lastly, Derek heads up north to Wales's largest island, Anglesey, where he visits another tiny island with a secluded chapel, an unexpected motor racing track, a neolithic burial chamber and a sauna on a beach.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt dishes up a feast of food from the Saturday Kitchen archives to whet the appetite for the week ahead. The Hairy Bikers bring comfort food bang up to date with sticky Szechuan lamb, stuffed into pillowy soft bao buns, with a fresh hit of pickled carrots, spring onion and herbs – cosy comfort with a fragrant Asian twist! Meera Sodha introduces a taste of Sri Lanka to the studio as she continues the comfort theme with her warming lentil and coconut dal with crispy mustard kale. Jeremy Lee brings his effervescent charm and wit to the kitchen whilst giving an underused cut of meat its chance in the spotlight. He makes a rich steamed kid pudding that melts in the mouth. Mary McCartney celebrates Bonfire Night with her flavour-packed smoky dogs, while Carmen O’Neal and Idris Elba team up to serve a masterclass in brandy. And queen of puddings Nigella Lawson tucks into either her food heaven, scallops, or her food hell, candied fruit. Meanwhile, Rick Stein explores the New Forest's bounty of produce, and the Hairy Bikers make a Menorcan dish in the Mediterranean Sea.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Sitting between Germany and France, Alsace is frontier land with a cuisine to match. In Strasbourg, Eva stops off at Brasserie Le Tigre for a beer (brassier means ‘to brew’) and a deliciously creamy tarte flambee. Then there's a trip to guide Coralie Andt’s restaurant, known as a winstub, where French wines can be enjoyed with plenty of cheese and sausage – as well as more sausage with sauerkraut cooked in white Riesling wine. With French tarts in a brasserie that serves German-style beer, and German sausage in a winstub serving French white wine, Alsace is defined by its competing national influences.

programme.title: Best Bakes Ever
programme.desc: With Britain more obsessed with baking than ever, actress and cake expert Jane Asher brings together a selection of recipes from the nation's favourite television chefs, for Best Bakes Ever. Each episode gives baking fans another chance to experience classic dishes from the likes of the James Martin, Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood, the Hairy Bikers, Raymond Blanc, Nigella Lawson, Tom Kerridge, Lorraine Pascale and Rachel Khoo. There's added insight and appreciation from Jane herself too. Whether its cakes, pies, puddings or main courses - this greatest hits of baking is a must for anyone with a need to knead, and should help inspire even more of us to start getting creative in the kitchen.

programme.title: I Was Monty's Double
programme.desc: World War II drama. A low-ranking officer who resembles General Montgomery is recruited to play his double in an elaborate plan to trick the Nazis.

programme.title: Women's Super League
programme.desc: Women's Super League action as Charlton Athletic face Chelsea.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin introduces a collection of the best finds from the show's travels to Lulworth Castle in Dorset, Chiddingstone Castle in Kent, and Wrest Park in Bedfordshire. The antiques experts include Catherine Southon, Christina Trevanion, Adam Partridge, Mark Stacey and Thomas Plant, with items ranging from a cloisonne vase to an astonishing collection of First World War slides. Paul also finds out more about the ancient art of shipbuilding at Buckler's Hard in Hampshire.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: For a live demonstration of terroir, Eva heads to Domaine Dujac, home of the current most-wanted Burgundy wine. Standing on one side of a road, owner Jeremy Seysses points to a parcel of grand cru (the very best) of Clos de la Roche. On the other side is a premier cru (the next best) - a Gevrey-Chambertin Combottes. Back at the winery, Eva tucks into beef cheeks bathed in Domaine Dujac for a classic boeuf bourguignon lunch. Despite the grapes being grown just a few metres away, these reds are a class apart.

programme.title: Wild Horses, the Rockies and Me
programme.desc: Gordon Buchanan heads to the Rocky Mountains in search of wild horses. Finding two stallions battling over a herd, Gordon immerses himself in their world, hoping to win their trust.

programme.title: BBC Young Musician
programme.desc: Who will be crowned the winner? Three virtuosic performers vie for the coveted title in a thrilling concert at Bristol Beacon. Presented by Petroc Trelawny.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob are back in Norfolk - a bittersweet return, as this was the very first location where Ted joined them. They both reminisce about Ted and raise a cup in his memory - although Ted would have preferred a biscuit. They head to some prime Norfolk lakes, hoping to catch a bream. It’s been well documented that Bob is not a fan of the bream, but will a big catch make him change his tune? It's Paul and Bob's birthday week, and they consider whether they may celebrate any further milestones or simply let them pass. Bob ends up throwing a surprise 70s-themed birthday party for Paul on the roof of the Blickling Estate, once owned by the Boleyn family.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: Irish film star Chris O'Dowd joins Bill Murray and his friend Tom Coyne for a lively round of golf, with enthusiasm occasionally outstripping ability. Away from the fairways, a traditional rambling house takes Bill outside his comfort zone as he explores Ireland's rich storytelling traditions. Later, in a packed Irish pub, the music starts – and staying on the sidelines proves impossible.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools welcomes Skepta, Jordan Rakei, Bloc Party, Johnny and Lillie Flynn, corto.alto and Rita Wilson.

programme.title: Walk the Line
programme.desc: The story of the legendary country artist Johnny Cash, from his early days on an Arkansas cotton farm to his rise to fame with Sun Records and his long association with singer June Carter, later to become his wife.

programme.title: Ellie & Natasia
programme.desc: A routine driving lesson takes a bizarre, surreal turn; a game show called Find the Snakes is destined to sweep the nation; contemporary politicians are introduced to a literal public arena; vape sommeliers treat e-liquid profiles with the gravity of a fine Bordeaux; two ultra-wealthy girls are determined to get exactly what they want; and two restaurant-goers take their love of food to an intense extreme. Featuring an appearance from Asim Chaudry.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Following this week’s Labour Budget, Fiona Bruce presents an hour of debate from Warwick. On the panel are chief secretary to the treasury, Labour’s Emma Reynolds MP; Conservative James Cartlidge MP; Liberal Democrat Daisy Cooper MP; Reform UK’s Zia Yusuf; and podcaster and author Alastair Campbell. They debate the Budget, Brexit and debt from student loans.

programme.desc: Today Flog It! comes from Glemham Hall in the Suffolk countryside. Antiques experts James Lewis and David Fletcher find a selection of antiques and collectibles to take to auction. There’s a Flog It first when James uncovers a copy of a Raphael painting saved by a Jewish professor who fled Hitler’s regime, and David Fletcher spots a rare flintlock pistol. Paul Martin visits a Cold War airbase to find out what life was like for American airmen based in the UK.

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor kicks off the week by chatting to the latest couple to be eliminated from the competition. Also, Friday’s all-star panel return to look back at the weekend’s spooky performances.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Jonathan Head reports from Thailand, where recent flooding has highlighted the growing challenges facing Bangkok. As climate change brings rising seas and more extreme weather across South East Asia, we examine why the Thai capital is among the region's most vulnerable cities. Plus: BBC Eye investigates the shadow war being fought inside Russia, speaking to two Russian men who claim to have secretly worked for Ukraine's intelligence services. Through rare first-hand accounts, we explore a clandestine world of covert operations, sabotage and espionage targeting military personnel and infrastructure far from the battlefield.

It’s a knockout round, and only one of the two returning teams can go through after trying to establish what connects such apparently random clues as Bradypus tridactylus, ‘Sunflower Seeds’ artist, Anguilla and Grok.

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: The second round of the competition begins. Two teams of students go head-to-head for a place in the quarter-finals. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc: In September 1972, one month after dictator Idi Amin announces his plan to expel all Ugandan Asians from the country, 80,000 people are making plans to flee, in fear for their lives. Maz and Bharti head for the capital Kampala, where hundreds gather, desperate to find out whether their British passports will be enough to escape to Britain. As the deadline approaches, Harminder’s father escapes arrest and schoolboy Paresh hides during overnight curfews while gunfire echoes across the city. Britain is divided. Controversial politician Enoch Powell rallies those who say the Ugandan Asians have no right to come, a newspaper poll finds just six per cent of the public want them here, and some councils try to steer new arrivals away from their cities. In Uganda, Amin refuses to negotiate – stepping up the pressure on those stuck in the country.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: Tim Renkow welcomes comedians Janine Harouni and Stuart Goldsmith to the stage.

programme.title: Newsnight

programme.desc: A brutal murder in an Inverness home sparks a manhunt for two violent suspects. Detectives recover crucial evidence beside a canal and track down CCTV, but the case takes a strange turn when they begin to doubt their main eyewitness. On Lewis, police face a stand-off with a camper van driver who insists the law doesn’t apply to her. And in the Cairngorms, an upturned canoe triggers a search for a missing man.

programme.title: Fallen Leaves
programme.desc: Comedy romance set in modern-day Helsinki. A lonely metalworker and a single woman working as a supermarket shelf stacker meet by chance in a karaoke bar. Drawn to each other, they strike a quiet yet immediate connection. Along their uneven path to happiness lie lost phone numbers, mistaken addresses, alcoholism and a charming stray dog. Aki Kaurismäki's Nordic comedy romance, winner of the Cannes Festival Jury Prize. In Finnish with English subtitles.

programme.desc: A stone’s throw from today’s antiques fair in West Sussex is a 500-acre wild botanic garden with an exquisite Elizabethan mansion at its centre. Natasha Raskin Sharp takes a break from the hustle and bustle of the fair to visit Kew Wakehurst and learn of its long history. The mansion’s roof has just been restored, and inside Natasha meets one of the curators to find out about several objects recently uncovered that tell of this grand house’s story. Over the fence, niece and aunt Abby and Della take on dad and daughter Sonal and Ruhi on a sweep of the antiques stalls, with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester in tow. With a few buys under their belts, the reds recline on a pair of furry blue armchairs, but the punchy price tag means they don’t stop for long. The blues also have furniture on their minds when Ruhi spots an occasional table – made from a tree trunk. In Chichester, the teams plan to grow a profit when Nick Hall takes to the rostrum. Caroline hopes her bonus buy will bring Abby and Della good luck, while Thomas aims to spread the love with his.

programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: Did you know that the Victorians invented films? Not only that, but one of the first stars of the moving image was Queen Victoria! Using real footage recently restored by the BFI, this special show takes a Horribly Historical look at the Victorians’ obsession with film. We see some of Queen Vicky’s very first filmic appearances (also featuring an initially reluctant Tsar Nicholas I), and also how the Victorians became obsessed with filming everything, from their holidays abroad to strapping cameramen to the front of a moving train (using only ropes) to make ‘Phantom Ride’ films. Along the way we also meet the Lumiere brothers (one of whom looks a lot like First Dates' Fred Sirieix), Kaiser Wilhelm II, notable Victorian actor Herbert Beerbohm Tree, and we see that the Victorians were also early adopters of Fake News. The episode ends with a show-stopping song that traces the evolution of film from the Victorians’ first forays through to the blockbusters we see in the multiplexes today.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Plastic is one of the greatest inventions in human history. It makes so much of our lives possible, but how we dispose of it is now a massive problem. By the year 2050 it’s thought that there will be more plastic than fish in our seas. So what can we do about it? First, ditch the disposable plastic water bottle and go for tap water in a reusable bottle. Better for the environment and cheaper too! Next, join a beach clean. It may seem like this problem is too big for us to handle but many hands make light work. Reduce, reuse and, importantly, recycle. And even more importantly than that, don’t drop litter. A bag that is thrown on the streets of London could end up on the coast of Africa or in the belly of a whale or a turtle. Lastly and most importantly, know that every single person can make a difference. One single plastic bag could choke a turtle or sunfish. One plastic straw could be the end of a gorgeous, iconic animal, so know you have power and use it.
